author: Cyrus
message:
Fetcher hardening: single GET, author name cleanup, PDF cache verification

R13 (#22): Replace HEAD+GET with single streaming GET in web_fetcher.
  Halves roundtrips per fetch; eliminates HEAD/GET content-type disagreement.

R16 (#25): Strip honorifics and suffixes in arXiv author name parsing.
  Dr./Prof. stripped from forenames; Jr./Sr./II-IV stay with surname.

R7 (#16): Verify cached PDFs before returning them.
  Adds _cached_pdf_is_valid() helper (magic bytes + 1 KB min size) to
  arxiv_fetcher cache-hit path; extends existing %PDF check in doi_fetcher
  with size guard; adds pre-write validation to web_fetcher _handle_pdf_from_url.
  Corrupt/truncated caches are deleted and re-fetched instead of blindly trusted.

author: Cyrus
message:
Atomic state writes + corrupt-state backup (closes #11)

Addresses the "data-loss pair" (M4 + M5) from the 2026-04-22 adversarial
code review.

Previously:

- StateManager.save() called Path.write_text, which truncates-then-writes.
  An interrupt or crash mid-write could leave processing_state.json empty
  or partial.
- StateManager._load_state() fell back to an empty ProcessingState on ANY
  parse failure, logging only at WARNING. A truncated state file therefore
  silently wiped the processed-papers record, and the next run would
  reprocess everything: API budget burned, duplicate vault notes produced.

Changes:

- save() serializes to a sibling .tmp file, then os.replace() into place.
  os.replace is atomic on POSIX (and Windows, when src and dst share a
  filesystem, which is guaranteed here since both live in the same dir).
- _load_state() on parse failure now copies the corrupt bytes to
  processing_state.corrupt.<epoch> and logs at ERROR so the situation is
  surfaced in telemetry. If the backup copy itself fails, that too is
  logged at ERROR rather than swallowed.

Tests (tests/test_state.py, new, 8 cases):

- Atomic: save produces parseable file; no stray .tmp left behind;
  overwrites are atomic; and — critically — if the tmp write fails mid-
  save, the original good file is preserved byte-for-byte.
- Backup: corrupt JSON is copied to a .corrupt.* sibling before reset;
  load still falls back to an empty state so the pipeline keeps running;
  missing file (first run) does NOT create a spurious backup; valid
  round-trip doesn't either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Cyrus
message:
Delete batch_process.py; batch is now handled by alcanzai CLI (closes #27)

paper_library/batch_process.py was functionally redundant with the
`alcanzai batch` Click command in cli.py. Two code paths for the same
feature had drifted in style — CLI uses structlog + Click output, the
standalone script still used print() (missed in the v0.2.5 structlog
sweep).

Verified no external automation referenced it:
  grep batch_process across repo → only doc/log entries + the file itself
  No CI workflow, shell script, or cron reference.

Docs updated:
- CLAUDE.md module table: row removed
- README.md directory tree: entry removed

Closes #27 (R18: cleanup).

author: Cyrus
message:
Add issue templates for epic / feature / bug / design-question

Bare-bones issue-tracking scaffolding to support the pbjson-for-why /
deciduous-for-what / issues-for-how-and-when memory model. Templates
nudge each new issue toward its canonical shape: design questions
include options + blocked-by; epics include sub-issue checklists + open
questions; features include a parent-epic link.

config.yml disables blank issues and surfaces the live decision graph
viewer as a contact link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
